analysis.title: GS Vol Views 7 Oct 2026
key_insights: Index vols remain low versus history after a record-high S&P close on Tuesday. Whether they are cheap is debated given compressed realized vol and system leverage. Drivers include subdued sentiment and positioning in cash and vol, and increased dispersion between AI leaders and rate-sensitive laggards.
Semis near-dated vols are below the 20th percentile versus the past 2 years across several names, as option players focus on CPU and Muse-adjacent dynamics.

Index skew was crushed, especially in the front end, as the market closed at all-time highs Tuesday, but caught a strong bid Wednesday morning. GS estimates the market is trading around a pocket of dealer long gamma, which dampens realized moves in either direction.
Cross-asset correlations between equities, rates and energy are changing materially from one session to the next (chart of ES1 vs US10Y).

Uranium: headlines this week confirm acceleration of the domestic nuclear buildout ($120bn US-Korea strategic build, $4.2bn conditional DOE loan for Vistra, Google 890 MW Constellation deal). Positioning in the GS uranium basket (GSXURANI) is at structural lows, which GS calls a clean tactical entry via index or URA call spreads.

Semis: after a two-month pullback driven by significant de-risking, GIR sees a more constructive setup into earnings. It expects AMAT to raise margin targets and give DRAM/logic commentary at SEMICON West in October, and CDNS to benefit from agentic AI synergies and possibly raise 2026 guidance.

SPCX: GIR reiterated Buy ahead of 17 Nov earnings and raised the 12-month PT to $230. It argues AI segment estimates look conservative versus Street over the next 6-18 months. Vol is at the lows since options listed on 16 June.

VIX: vol of vol (VVIX) has collapsed to near its August lows and asset managers are at record net-short VIX futures, beyond July 2024 extremes, while S&P positioning is still elevated. GS says this explains why vol has not reacted to recent equity selloffs and leaves the VIX complex vulnerable to a squeeze. It expects vol to stay sticky or drift higher into the November expiry.

Breadth: the rolling 30-day return gap between SPX and SPXXAI is near its widest since January 2023, and the % of stocks above their 50-day average has turned higher over the past few days. GS sees a possible start of a breadth recovery.

Brazil: EWZ has rallied 13% since Flavio Bolsonaro's surprise election showing, with $700mm of EWZ creation, the largest daily inflow on record, reversing the August $2.7bn redemption wave. GS customers added downside via EWZ puts.

Dispersion has been one of 2026's most discussed derivative trades. Implied correlation is near historical lows and realized correlation fell further because single-stock earnings moves beat implied pricing (AMZN, MSFT, NVDA). Flow is two-way and GS can facilitate vanilla options on implied dispersion.

The SPX top 50 singles minus index implied vol spread has fallen sharply from July record highs, with steep drops in AI-related names (MU, SNDK, AMD). Clients sold dispersion when the spread was near highs, and some are now buying singles vol and selling index vol to defend the theme.

China: funding spreads on onshore AI hardware proxies (CSI 300) are quite negative, with flow into calls, call spreads and floored swaps. GS cites washed-out positioning, Q2 EPS growth of +20% YoY, record negative funding, cheap vol, and smaller AI hardware stocks migrating into the CSI 300.
